title: Saved query scopes: named, reusable document selections
summary: Saved scopes are named, reusable document selections that a member creates from the Documents catalog and reuses as the scope when asking questions or starting chats. This plan adds a `query_scopes` table scoped to workspace + owner, a workspace store modeled on SourceLibraryStore, a five-endpoint JSON API, and picker/save wiring in the vanilla-JS Ask, Chat, and Documents pages. Per your choices: scopes are private to their creator, they reach Ask, Chat, and the Documents save flow, and a saved list with a since-deleted document fails the run through the existing strict scope-resolution error, with the UI prompting an edit. No new scope kinds and no changes to the answer or chat pipelines — a saved scope expands into the exact same QueryScope payload the client sends today.

src/api/research-thread-routes.ts:54-118 — the route module pattern (services.run, requireRequestPrincipal, WebRequestError mapping) that query-scope-routes.ts should copy.
src/api/services.ts:1056-1061 and 994-999 — how listSourceLibraries/createSharedSourceLibrary wire a store through manager.withRuntime; saved-scope services follow this.

steps.what: Add the query_scopes table and its drizzle schema + migration
steps.why: Every other persisted user artifact (threads, conversations, libraries) lives in drizzle-managed tables with the same workspace/user FK pattern; saved scopes need the same durability and the same cascade behavior on user or workspace deletion.
steps.detail:
New table `query_scopes` in src/database/schema.ts and a checked-in migration file drizzle/0021_query_scopes.sql:

| column | type | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | uuid | pk |
| workspace_id | uuid | not null, FK workspaces(id) on delete cascade |
| owner_user_id | uuid | not null, FK users(id) on delete cascade |
| name | text | not null |
| scope | jsonb | not null, stores the existing QueryScope union |
| created_at / updated_at | timestamptz | not null, default now |

Indexes: unique on (workspace_id, owner_user_id, sql`lower(trim(name))`), index on (owner_user_id, workspace_id).

steps.what: Create QueryScopeStore in src/workspaces/query-scope-store.ts with listForPrincipal, readForPrincipal, createForPrincipal, updateForPrincipal, deleteForPrincipal
steps.why: Mirrors the existing SourceLibraryStore placement and conventions; all queries filter on workspace_id AND owner_user_id = principal.userId so cross-owner access is impossible by construction. create validates name (nonempty, <=200 chars) and the payload with queryScopeSchema; update raises a conflict error when the name collides with a different scope in the same workspace+owner; missing rows raise the store's own error type mapped to 404 at the route layer.

steps.what: Add request decoders, the /api/query-scopes route module, and WebServices entries
steps.why: Decoders live in src/api/request-boundary.ts next to decodeQuestionRequest and decodeCreateResearchThreadRequest; routes follow the research-thread-routes.ts shape exactly (services.run + requireRequestPrincipal); services.ts gains listQueryScopes/createQueryScope/readQueryScope/updateQueryScope/deleteQueryScope constructed from the store inside manager.withRuntime. Route registration is added in server.ts buildWebServer alongside the other modules.

steps.what: Add web/assets/scripts/query-scopes.js (+ .d.ts) with boundary readers and picker-state helpers, imported by app.js
steps.why: Boundary readers follow the readNonEmptyString/readPlainObject discipline of boundary-readers.js; helpers fetch the summary list, load one scope's full definition, and compute the picker options. Adding .d.ts matches document-notifications.d.ts.

steps.what: Add a "Saved scopes" section to the Ask and Chat scope pickers
steps.why: On pick, the client loads the scope definition (GET /api/query-scopes/:id), then carries it as the ordinary scope payload — the strict resolution of documentIds in src/documents/catalog/query-scope.ts:27 gives the agreed error-and-prompt behavior without server changes. On scope-resolution failure, the UI offers 'Edit saved scope' when the failing scope came from the picker. Ask's changeScope (ask.js:696-705) gains the saved-scope branch; Chat's new-conversation form gains the same options.

steps.what: Add a "Save selection as scope" action on the Documents multi-select with a small name modal
steps.why: The hand-off to Ask/Chat already carries the current selection; the same state is what the save action posts. After saving, the page confirms and links to Ask. Documents with no selection keep the action disabled.

steps.what: Add test/query-scope-store.test.ts (CRUD, owner isolation, name validation/conflict, zod scope validation), test/query-scope-boundary.test.ts (decoders + web readers), and route-level cases in test/web-server.test.ts
steps.why: Matches the existing split between store tests, boundary tests, and web-server route tests; owner-isolation is the security-critical property and gets direct coverage.

steps.what: Document saved scopes in docs/features.md under the Ask/Chat sections
steps.why: features.md is the feature reference the Help page links to; a short subsection covering private visibility, strict resolution on deleted documents, and the Save-selection flow keeps the docs honest.

assumptions: No migration tooling beyond the existing `pnpm db:generate` flow is needed; the new table is added as a checked-in drizzle migration 0021.
The Ask/Chat pages submit a saved scope by expanding it client-side into the existing QueryScope payload; the server question and conversation endpoints themselves stay unchanged.
Saved-scope names are unique per owner and workspace; renaming is a PATCH on the scope row.
verification:
1. `pnpm exec vitest run test/query-scope-store.test.ts test/query-scope-boundary.test.ts` — new unit tests pass.
2. `pnpm test:integration` (with `pnpm services:test:up`) — store CRUD and migration apply against a real PostgreSQL; `test/web-server.test.ts` cases cover route behavior.
3. `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint` — boundary `.d.ts` and new modules are clean.
4. `pnpm db:migrate` — migration 0021 applies to the development database.
5. For the user: run `pnpm dev:web` and `pnpm worker`, select documents in Documents → "Save selection as scope" → pick the saved scope in Ask and in a new Chat conversation; delete a saved-scope document and re-ask to confirm the resolution error appears with the "Edit saved scope" prompt.

The project has a `.claims/` setup with no claims yet; after implementation each touched store/route behavior that carries a guarantee (owner isolation, 404-not-leak, name validation) gets a `// claim(...)` line proposed with a break, per the claims-writing skill, and `claims impact` runs before finishing.
